prompt:
You are an experienced sommelier comparing two wine recommenders. A
customer with no wine knowledge made this request:

"Can you help me find a strong, heavy sweet white wine that tastes like peach and spices for a cheese board?"

List A:
Wine 1: Pinot Grigio, US, $10. Tasting note: "This is a sweet, softly simple wine whose apricot, citrus and peach flavors will satisfy those looking for a decent everyday white wine."
Wine 2: Riesling, US, $9. Tasting note: "If you like your white wines fruity and sweet, this one's for you. It has pretty flavors of peaches, honey and spices."
Wine 3: Marsanne, US, $12. Tasting note: "Here's a ripe, complex white wine with aromas and flavors ranging from tangerines, apricots and bananas to malted chocolate milk. It tastes very ripe and fruity, with a soft, creamy mouthfeel like peach syrup. There might be just a tad of residual sugar in there, but it's basically a dry wine."
Wine 4: Cortese, US, $18. Tasting note: "A little heavy and soft for a white wine, but shows true dryness and some interestingly earthy flavors of white tobacco, herbs and citrus fruits. Promising, but needs greater structure and complexity."
Wine 5: Albana, Italy, price unknown. Tasting note: "This is a beautiful and delicate dessert wine with lightly musty notes that appear in the back of candied fruit, orange zest, almond paste, stone fruit and vanilla cream. It feels light and buoyant on the close but also delivers the heft and personality you need for a pairing with aged goat cheese and apricot jelly."

List B:
Wine 1: Riesling, US, $9. Tasting note: "If you like your white wines fruity and sweet, this one's for you. It has pretty flavors of peaches, honey and spices."
Wine 2: Sauvignon Blanc, US, $16. Tasting note: "This interesting and rather subtle wine smells like white pepper and pistachios and tastes like white peaches. It stays dry on the palate, while the texture spreads flavors smoothly for a sense of richness."
Wine 3: Viognier, US, $22. Tasting note: "Aromas of white peach and vanilla highlight this rich-textured, rather full-bodied white wine. It's made in a generous rather than crisp style, as if it were barrel fermented, and a buttery lushness defines it more than the fairly subtle fruit flavors. Very tasty overall."
Wine 4: Riesling, US, $18. Tasting note: "This has aromas of yellow peach and butter. Straightforward flavors faintly resemble peach, with more of the buttery richness that seems unusual for this variety. It's a good, basic, full-bodied white wine."
Wine 5: Moschofilero, Greece, $19. Tasting note: "Elegant white rose and peach aromas lead this delicate white from Greece. Fresh peach, grapefruit and delicate spice on the palate give the wine pretty poise. Overall, a great example of how refined the Greek wines can be."

Which list answers the request better as a whole: relevance to every wish,
variety where the request leaves room, and fit for any occasion? If they
are equally good, say tie. Think briefly, then answer with JSON only:
{"reason": "<two sentences at most>", "better": "A" | "B" | "tie"}
